newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond volatility gets pummeled.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond volatility gets pummeled.

text.p: Implied volatilities for Treasury bond options sank after the U.S. released April employment numbers, and some traders expected the post-report funk to linger in the absence of much new data next week.
June bond volatility fell 0.7 point from its opening level to 8.15 percent late in Friday's session, traders said. It was off about 0.45 point from the settlement Thursday.
Minutes after the jobs report was released, volatility in June had dropped as low as 7.40 percent. "It got whacked," said a trader on the CBOT floor.

Traders who put on bearish speculative positions before the jobs numbers were disappointed. One brokerage house bought 8,000 June 106-00 puts, paying 3/64, just before the 0730 CDT release, hoping for a big downmove, floor sources said.
But bond futures shot up in the aftermath of the report, keying off the lower than expected 142,000 growth in nonfarm payrolls.
The 0.3 point decline in the unemployment rate to a 4.9 percent, the lowest level since 1973, eventually tempered the market's bullish enthusiasm.
At the close, Treasury bond futures were 8/32 higher at 109-29, and September Eurodollar futures were unchanged at 93.885.
Next week's light economic calendar promises to keep a lid on interest rate volatility, market participants said.
"Without a whole lot of numbers out, we'll probably stay pretty low," said the CBOT trader.

In Eurodollar options, volatilities were flat to lower, with September 93.75 straddles unchanged at 10.00 percent, December at 93.75 straddles down 0.9 point at 11.50 percent and March 93.50 straddles down 0.8 point at 13.30 percent.
A Eurodollar options analyst said volatility spreads in those months were converging after deferred values had grown especially rich versus the front months.
